newsitem.title: UK: Advertising exec says UK pay-TV remains secondary.
newsitem.headline: Advertising exec says UK pay-TV remains secondary.

text.p: Pay television remains a secondary medium in Britain, with terrestrial television continuing to claim 92 percent of all viewing in the country, an advertising executive said on Monday.

"In spite of the advent of satellite and cable TV, only 23 percent of households have as yet taken up these options," Jennifer Laing, chairman of Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising, told the annual conference of the Confederation of British Industry. "And 92 percent of all television viewing is still terrestrial. It is worth remembering that ITV continues to be the only intrusive way for advertisers to reach large, mass audiences."
ITV is the larger of Britain's two, commercial, terrestrial television networks.

Laing also told business leaders that they must work to protect their brands, because brands hold the key for future corporate profits. "Nothing can be more important to the company chairman for the protection of future profits than protecting and exploiting the essence of the brand," she said.
